subject: 2 basic questions on minutes per day

messages.author: c1458cffc41a00c5
messages.subject: 2 basic questions on minutes per day
parts:
Good afternoon,

I am a beginer in GGIR. I only need to analyze data from 6:00 am to midnight 00:00. I will not take into account sleep hours nor sleep analysis.  

I have tried to specify this in the shell function:
....

includedaycrit = 10,  

  qwindow=c(6,24),      

  mvpathreshold =c(143),      

  boutcriter = 0.9,      

  mvpadur= c(1,5,10),            

  bout.metric = 4,            

  def.noc.sleep = c(24,6),   

  outliers.only = TRUE,     

  criterror = 4,            

  includenightcrit=16,        

  threshold.lig = c(63),  

  threshold.mod = c(143),  

  threshold.vig = c(465),

  boutcriter.in = 0.9,        

  boutcriter.lig = 0.9,

  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.9, 

  boutdur.in = c(1,5,10),   

  boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10),

  boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),        

  timewindow = c("MM"),     

  includedaycrit.part5= 2/3,        

  part5_agg2_60seconds=TRUE

....

My questions are:

1- Wich columns I have to look for to find the

minutes per day of MVPA, min per day of light, min per day of sedentary time, mean ECMO, and the same variables in bouts?

2.- is it normal that in children of 7 to 9 years old the mean ECMO is around  50? I find this very low, since the cutt-points for MVPA is almost 200¡ 


Thank you very much in advance¡¡¡¡

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] 2 basic questions on minutes per day
parts:
Hi Gabriela,

Re. question 1: See https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#4_Inspecting_the_results for guidance on variable names in the output reports. If you need more support then options may be: 1) Post back here the variable names you are planning to use and what you want to use them for, and hope that someone provides feedback, 2) Seek collaboration with a group that has worked with GGIR before, e.g. Granada group by Fran Ortega in Granada, 3) Hire me to give you an introduction course on GGIR, send me a personal message for more info.

Re. question 2: Average movement is usually lower than the MVPA threshold, because most of our time we spent in sleep or inactivity. Whether 50 is a normal value for your population is probably best to check by comparison with literature, e.g. check out the studies by Lynne Boddy or the studies by da Silva (Pelotas 2004 cohort).

Best wishes,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant

Hello Vincent, 
I am finally using output part 5 for the analysis.  I have some last questions. 
As I told you in previous emails, Im am only working with data from 6:00 to 24:00. I am using this shell:

g.shell.GGIR(
  mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),                            
  datadir="Y:/WS_INMA/INMA_DATA/Actigraph/Gipuzkoa/mydata",  
  outputdir="Y:/WS_INMA/INMA_DATA/Actigraph/Gipuzkoa/gab_myresults_prueba_PA",          
  overwrite=FALSE,                             
  windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),    
  do.enmo = TRUE,                                                  
  desiredtz= "Europe/Madrid",
  strategy = 1,        
  hrs.del.start = 2,    
  hrs.del.end = 2,      
  maxdur = 9,          
  includedaycrit = 10,  
  qwindow=c(6,24),      
  mvpathreshold =c(191.6),      
  boutcriter = 0.8,      
  mvpadur= c(1,5,10),            
  excludefirstlast = FALSE,  
  def.noc.sleep = c(24,6),  
  ignorenonwear=TRUE,

excludefirstlast = FALSE,
  includenightcrit=16,    
  threshold.lig = c(56.3),  
  threshold.mod = c(191.6),  
  threshold.vig = c(695.8),
  boutcriter.in = 0.9,        
  boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,

boutdur.in = c(1,5,10),    
  boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),        
  timewindow = c("MM"),

excludefirstlast.part5= FALSE,    
  includedaycrit.part5= 0.58,          
  part5_agg2_60seconds=TRUE,        
  minimum_MM_length.part5=23,        
  do.report=c(2,5),          
  viewingwindow=1 ,        
  visualreport=TRUE) 
 
My questions are: 
1) I noticed that , even after indicating maxdur = 9,  in the results part 2 I get : n.days.of.measurement.after.which.all.data.is.ignored..if.strategy.1.= 7. Why is this?

2) I indicated  minimum_MM_length.part5=23, this means part 5 results only include days with (valid or invalid) data on at least 23  hours, right?

3) I used boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8 because using 1 gives me a cero number of bouts. Now, when using 0.8, I get the results for "AD_MVPA_E5S_B10M100._T143_ENMO_6.24hr",  "AD_MVPA_E5S_B1M100._T143_ENMO_6.24hr",  "AD_MVPA_E5S_B5M100._T143_ENMO_6.24hr". All cero again, and it does not give the results for M80. What am I doing wrong?

4) is it normal to get NA in the time stamp variables? (AD_qwindow_timestamps, WE_qwindow_timestamps, and so on). Or is it an error?

I apologise if my questions are way to basic¡

Thank you very much.
